items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I worked as a bus boy at a place called LaRue’s

ctx.x: I’m not sure I had a plan. When I was in high school, I worked at night. I worked as a bus boy at a place called LaRue’s and another place called The Plantation and several of the clubs. So I worked – when I would get out of school, I would go straight there at 4 o’clock. I would work from 4 to midnight, and then I would take my tuba or trombone, and I would go sit in until 3 in the morning and then get up at 7 o’clock and start school again. I can remember Mr. Morton-Finney – I was taking French, and the only…

LaRue’s Supper Club. I would come up there. I would have my little busboy jacket. They let me play Lullaby of the Leaves with the band. They thought that was something, because they would let – and unfortunately there I had another friend working there – a busboy – who had a wonderful voice. He was very, very dark- skinned.
